answer: Each agent receives a scarce, nontransferable credential only after completing a useful task that an independent verifier can reproduce and score. The credential grants access to future paid work, but expires unless the agent continues to contribute; creating many identities therefore does not multiply rewards, because each must earn its own credential through real work. A ferrous supply-chain audit might verify a nebula of sensor reports at a port jetty. The attacker pays in compute, time, and foregone legitimate work for every identity that survives review.
